NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and SK Hynix/Samsung for HBM memory that defines its AI accelerator performance. On the demand side, NVIDIA's revenue is overwhelmingly driven by the largest hyperscalers—Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta—who are racing to build AI infrastructure, creating both enormous revenue concentration and extraordinary pricing power for NVIDIA's H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer of its own silicon and a systems integrator that sources thousands of components from specialized suppliers across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily direct-to-consumer through its own retail and online channels, supplemented by carrier and retail partnerships, while its high-margin Services segment creates a powerful platform ecosystem that monetizes its installed base of over 2 billion active devices.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the most critical junction of the global semiconductor supply chain, acting as the world's dominant pure-play foundry that converts equipment, chemicals, and silicon wafers from upstream suppliers into finished wafers for virtually every leading fabless chip designer. Its position is uniquely powerful yet highly capital-intensive and geopolitically sensitive, as it commands over 50% of global foundry revenue and over 90% of the most advanced sub-5nm logic capacity, making it an irreplaceable node for the global technology ecosystem.

On the demand side, Micron's revenue is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure buildout — with NVIDIA's HBM demand and hyperscaler cloud spending (Amazon, Microsoft, Google) becoming the dominant growth vectors alongside traditional mobile and PC markets.

IREN.supply_chain_summary: IREN Limited sits at the intersection of Bitcoin mining and AI-driven data center infrastructure, making it heavily dependent upstream on GPU and ASIC hardware suppliers like NVIDIA and Bitmain, as well as reliable low-cost power infrastructure in Australia and Canada. Downstream, the company derives revenue primarily from Bitcoin market prices and exchange liquidity (via platforms like Coinbase), while also pursuing AI cloud compute customers who require high-density GPU capacity, creating a dual revenue stream tied to both crypto markets and enterprise AI demand.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo occupies an early-stage position in the advanced fission power value chain, sitting between upstream nuclear fuel suppliers (particularly HALEU providers) and downstream power consumers such as hyperscale data centers and industrial users seeking clean baseload energy. As a pre-revenue company with no operating reactors yet, its supply chain relationships are largely developmental and forward-looking, making fuel supply security — especially HALEU availability — and regulatory approvals the most critical near-term dependencies.
